option.label: Knotty base with densely hairy scale leaves
option.detail: Inspect scale-like leaves covering the firm crown. Their dense pubescence does not establish hairy culm nodes or underground runners.

option.label: LOWER sheaths densely felted with hairs
option.detail: Lower sheaths may be felty-pubescent in Gould, while other leaves are glabrous or sparsely hairy. Do not transfer the lower-sheath hair density to blades or nodes.

option.label: Narrow dense panicle; branches pressed toward axis
option.detail: Gould describes a narrow densely flowered panicle, usually with appressed, mostly simple branches. It can look fingerlike when branches separate.

option.label: UPPER glume densely silky, hairs 2–4 mm
option.detail: Find the second outer glume. Its long silvery or purple-tinged hairs are not stiff hairs on the first glume or an awn.

option.label: LOWER lemma margins densely silky, hairs 2–4 mm
option.detail: The lower floret margins carry long silvery or purple-tinged hairs. This is not the upper fertile lemma or a blade margin.

option.label: LOWER lemma back hairless
option.detail: Inspect the back separately from its densely hairy margins. The same lemma can have a hairless back and hairy edges.

option.label: UPPER lemma ovate to lance-shaped
option.detail: Gould describes the upper lemma as ovate-lanceolate, abruptly narrowing into a short awn tip. No smooth, shiny or hard texture is inferred.

option.label: UPPER lemma abruptly narrows to short awn tip
option.detail: Gould explicitly describes a short awn tip on the upper lemma. It has no measured length here. Keep it separate from the long 2–4 mm silky hairs.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Separate the silky hairs from the upper lemma tip

learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Do not use the hair length for a 2–5 mm fertile awn or infer KR’s bent, twisted awn.

diggs.confirmation: Named account confirms erect perennial, usually appressed dense digitate branches, glabrous blades and second-glume/lower-floret margin hairs 2–4 mm. Genus supplies two florets (lower staminate or neuter, upper fertile), minute/absent first glume and membranous ligule.
diggs.citation_history: Existing profile/evidence labels p.1263 as named account; preserved original records. Re-read footer places named account/key on1264 and genus on1263. New precise confirmation uses1264.

hill_country.retained: Existing flat blade, open sheath, lower hairy sheath, ligule1–3mm erose/truncate, erect culm and knotty base. Vegetative separation from D.insularis and D.patens unreliable.

secondary_reference_review.awn_disagreement: Gould short awn tip on upper lemma; older dossier cites awns absent and core none_obvious. Keep both reports; prioritize Gould for the newly supported short-awn observation, without calling silk hairs awns or inventing numerical length.
